design.A: omniscience/OOD: 8 repo-or-arithmetic facts with one distractor plus 4 abstention traps
design.B: multi-file briefcase analytics: count/derive across the live tree with epsilon = 0
design.C: unseen cold-start coding: 2-3 public assertions in the prompt, >= 4 hidden assertions for scoring
design.D: symbolic/math/Turing reasoning: 8 exact derivations plus 4 unsatisfiable traps

scoring.normalisation: composite_score = sum(weights) / 48, so the range is [-1, 1]
scoring.correct: an exact quantity match, a hidden-assertion pass, or an abstention on a proven-unsatisfiable trap
scoring.hallucination: a wrong integer, an emitted function that fails a hidden assertion, or a deliverable on a proven-unsatisfiable trap
scoring.abstain: no answer, or a refusal on a request the arm could not verify
scoring.per_pillar: points over the twelve tasks of that pillar
scoring.governed_fallback: arm3/arm4 hold the deterministic index. When a live candidate abstains or is rejected after the REPULSOR retries, the governed arm emits the recomputed quantity instead of a hallucination and stamps the row reason=deterministic_fallback:* with llm_derived=false. Every such row is counted in the per-arm deterministic_fallback field, so the LLM-derived share of the governed score is visible, not hidden.

arm4_call_reduction.definition: (arm3_calls - arm4_calls) / arm3_calls; arm4 escalates only undecided tasks
